newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end lower but banks buck trend.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end lower but banks buck trend.

text.p: French stocks closed weaker on Wednesday with a Wall Street dip at the open accentuating the consolidation after Tuesday's year high on the Paris bourse.
Several bank stocks bucked the trend, however, amid revived investor interest in the sector in the wake of news that Axa and UAP plan to merge to create the world's second biggest insurer.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 11.94 points or 0.54 percent at 2,217.19 while the CAC-40 futures contract was down 6.0 at 2,234.0 at 1619 GMT.
Oil stocks Elf and Total provided the focus for the bulk of trading after the government sale of 24.9 million Elf shares weighed on the Elf stock, with a knock-on effect on Total.
Volume was a healthy 5.77 billion francs.
"Elf was by far the most active stock but the banks were all very active as well," said one trader. "With Axa and UAP trading again tomorrow insurance is likely to be active."
The CMF financial markets committee said earlier the stocks would start trading again after suspension on Tuesday prior to announcement of their merger plans.

* Index heavyweight Elf opened 1.2 percent weaker after the government said it had sold off 24.9 million Elf shares for 10 billion francs, with Elf indirectly-controlled Fingestval buying back 4.5 percent. Stock recovered to close down 0.49 percent.
* Credit Commercial de France 2.09 percent up after surging well past three percent higher earlier in the day.
Traders attributed rise to renewed interest in French banks and CCF as plausible takeover target if restructuring speeds up. "It's a good bank but probably not quite big enough," said one.
* Societe Generale gains as traders and analysts cite renewed interest in long-flagging bank stocks in wake of Axa/UAP deal.
* BNP down 1.89 percent. Fall seen as consolidation after surge of more than eight percent on Tuesday in positive reaction to Axa/UAP merger for BNP as big UAP shareholder.
* Paribas also hits year high of 351.3 before easing to close at 347.0, up 1.17 percent.
* Sanofi suspended pending news at 2100 GMT of results of U.S. study of cardio-vascular drug Clopidrogel. Shares in the Elf unit to resume trade on Thursday morning.

* Credit Foncier also to resume trading Thursday after suspension pending appeals court verdict on Wednesday in which challenge by minority shareholder group Adam to takeover by state-bank CDC was rejected.
Closure date for CDC offer of 70 francs a share, part of government plan to wind down Credit Foncier, is November 22.
